description: TypeScript plumbing: thread the default-on emitLooseImages toggle and the new imagesDir/imagePaths/staleImagesRemoved outputs through the sidecar bridge and the psd_to_skeleton MCP tool, and cover it with jest. Covers plan.md items 7-8. Depends on FEAT-001 for the request key and response field names.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/context.json and this file first, then .agents/tasks/plan.md items 7-8 and FEAT-001's findings for the exact sidecar key names it shipped.

In src/tools/generate-tools.ts, extend PsdToSkeletonResult with imagesDir?: string, imagePaths?: string[] and staleImagesRemoved?: string[], each commented as omitted by an older sidecar or when the toggle is off.

Add emitLooseImages?: boolean | undefined to the psdToSkeleton args type and forward it into the callSidecar request with the existing ...(args.x === undefined ? {} : { x: args.x }) spread, so a call that omits it produces the same request bytes as today.

Add the matching zod input: emitLooseImages: z.boolean().optional().describe(...) stating that it defaults to true and that the images/ folder is what the Spine editor's File -> Import Data resolves attachments against, while the runtime and render_preview read the atlas instead. Extend the tool description string and the file header comment with the same fact.

Add summary lines in psdToSkeleton: one naming the images directory and the count of loose PNGs (use generated.data.imagePaths ?? [] and never inline a long filename list — the full list stays in structuredContent through ok(data, summary)); one naming the pruned files when staleImagesRemoved is non-empty; and one warning that editor import will not resolve attachments when imagesDir is missing or empty. Keep resolveWriteTarget as the only path gate and do not touch src/path-safety.ts, src/capability-gate.ts or src/preview-renderer.ts.

In src/sidecar.ts, extend the header comment's protocol note to mention the emitLooseImages request key and the image fields in the response. No behavioural change there — the bridge is request-shape agnostic.

In tests/unit/generate-tools.test.ts, add imagesDir/imagePaths/staleImagesRemoved to SIDECAR_DATA and add behavioural tests: the summary names the images folder and the PNG count; emitLooseImages: false is forwarded; omitting it leaves the request exactly as the existing toEqual test asserts; a sidecar response without the image fields still succeeds and the summary warns that editor import will not resolve; result.data.generated.imagePaths reaches the caller; a non-empty staleImagesRemoved is reported in the summary.
Run npm install (node_modules is absent in this worktree), then the verification commands, then commit locally staging only the files named above.
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` are both clean.
`npx jest tests/unit/generate-tools.test.ts` passes, including the pre-existing exact-request assertion, which proves omitting emitLooseImages leaves the sidecar request unchanged.
psd_to_skeleton exposes an optional boolean emitLooseImages input whose description states it defaults to true, and the tool summary reports the images directory and the number of loose PNGs.
A sidecar response lacking the image fields still returns ok, with a summary line warning that the Spine editor import will not resolve attachments.
findings:
SHIPPED SURFACE for FEAT-003 (docs) to match. Option name: the MCP input is `emitLooseImages` (z.boolean().optional(), no zod default — undefined is simply not forwarded, so the sidecar's own default ON applies and a call that omits it produces byte-identical request JSON to before; the pre-existing exact-request toEqual test still passes). Its describe() text states: writes loose per-attachment PNGs into an images/ folder next to the skeleton JSON, defaults to true, that folder is what the Spine editor's File -> Import Data resolves attachments against (<skeleton.images>/<attachmentName>.png, relative to the JSON), the atlas is not read on import while the runtime and render_preview read the atlas and ignore these files, and stale PNGs from an earlier run are pruned.

EXACT SUMMARY WORDING SHIPPED (docs should not contradict these three lines):
1. images present: `Images: <imagesDir> — <N> loose PNG(s) named after the attachments, which is what the Spine editor's File -> Import Data resolves against.` Note the em dash (—) and the literal `loose PNG(s)`. Inserted immediately after the `Atlas: ...` line, before the virtual-bones line.
2. images absent or empty (older sidecar, or toggle off): `No loose per-attachment images were written, so the Spine editor's File -> Import Data will not resolve attachments and the canvas will look empty. Re-run with emitLooseImages true (the default) to get them; the atlas path (runtime and render_preview) is unaffected.` This is the TS-side line and is distinct from (though consistent with) the Python pipeline warning FEAT-001 appends; when the toggle is off both appear, which is intentional.
3. staleImagesRemoved non-empty: `Stale images pruned from that folder: <names joined by ', '>. The editor resolves attachment names against the folder, so leftovers from an earlier run are removed rather than silently picked up.` Names only, per FEAT-001's contract.

PsdToSkeletonResult gained `imagesDir?: string`, `imagePaths?: string[]`, `staleImagesRemoved?: string[]` — all optional, each commented as omitted by an older sidecar / empty when the toggle is off. The tool code defaults them locally (`?? ''`, `?? []`) and never mutates generated.data, so `result.data.generated.imagePaths` is literally what the sidecar sent (undefined when absent) — asserted by a test. No filename list is ever inlined into the summary; the full imagePaths list reaches the caller only through structuredContent via ok(data, summary), so MAX_INLINE_DETAIL_CHARS is untouched.

The tool `description` string gained one sentence with the same editor-vs-runtime fact and `Set emitLooseImages false to skip them.`; the generate-tools.ts header comment gained the matching paragraph; src/sidecar.ts's header gained a protocol note naming the emitLooseImages request key, the three response fields and why PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 1. No behavioural change in sidecar.ts.

Files changed: src/tools/generate-tools.ts, src/sidecar.ts, tests/unit/generate-tools.test.ts. Untouched as required: src/path-safety.ts, src/capability-gate.ts, src/preview-renderer.ts; outDir still goes through resolveWriteTarget as the only path gate. Four new jest tests in tests/unit/generate-tools.test.ts (folder + count reported and no filename in the summary; emitLooseImages:false forwarded; image-field-less response still ok with the warning line; staleImagesRemoved reported), and SIDECAR_DATA now carries imagesDir/imagePaths/staleImagesRemoved with a new IMAGES_DIR constant.

Verification: `npm install` (node_modules was absent; completed, then a re-run reported up to date), `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` both clean, `npx jest tests/unit/generate-tools.test.ts` 17 passed, `npm test` 30 suites / 622 passed / 1 skipped. No Python or docs files touched; pytest not re-run in this feature.
